name: Malluch
overview: Malluch was a male descendant of Harim noted in the book of Ezra. His unique distinction in Scripture is that he was among those who had married a foreign wife, a matter addressed in the post-exilic community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity. No specific tribal affiliation or additional personal details are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Malluch means 'counselor' or 'king,' reflecting a title or role of guidance or authority. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries significant meaning within the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Malluch is explicitly identified as a descendant of Harim, establishing his familial lineage. Beyond this connection, Scripture does not provide further details about his family or relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Malluch's significance lies in his inclusion among those who had taken foreign wives, a situation that Ezra 10 highlights as problematic for the returned exiles seeking to uphold the covenant with God. His mention underscores the communal challenges faced in restoring faithfulness and obedience in Israel after the exile. Thus, Malluch serves as a representative figure in the narrative addressing intermarriage and covenantal faithfulness.
